subject: Estimating Density for multiple species in multiple strata

messages.author: 738d983729adbc9d
messages.subject: Estimating Density for multiple species in multiple strata
parts:
Hello,

I searched the archives and readings relevant to my data and was unable t=
o find an answer.

I have point transect data for many species of birds across 40 different =
strata (8 points in each strata, visited 4 times each in one season). I =
have followed the protocol in the Alldredge et al 2007 ms for multiple sp=
ecies analysis and have created 6 groups of species based on similarities=
in detection. I want to get Density values for each species in each str=
ata, but the only way I can figure to do this is to analyze each group of=
species (N =3D 6) in each strata individually (N =3D 40). I then post-s=
tratify by species to get the D estimates (using global detection fxns) a=
nd assess any covariates (using MCDS - observer, time of day, species, et=
c). This is all well and good except that it would take a VERY LONG time=
considering that each analysis takes me about 20 minutes... (40*6*20 =3D=
80 hours)! Also, some strata have fewer than 50 detections for some spe=
cies groups (this is an suburban landscape).

I have a feeling that there is an quicker/better way, and would appreciat=
e any feedback. Possibly conducting the analysis for the species groups =
as a whole and using the parameter estimates from MCDS model to manually =
estimate D for each species in each strata???

Thanks for any help you can provide. Hopefully I have provided enough in=
formation.

Lesley

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Estimating Density for multiple species in multiple strata
parts:
Lesley:

You are a little thin on points per stratum to produce convincing=20
measures of precision within each stratum. Nevertheless, you should be=20
able to streamline your analysis so it does not take as much time as you =

project.

The approach I might take would be largely as you suggest but perhaps=20
using a project template such that a set of models is automatically run=20
for each of your combinations of strata/species group. That would knock =

down the time per combination I presume (or at least automate it so you=20
can be doing something else). Is most of the 20 minutes per analysis=20
spent setting up the models, or actually having the computer do the fitti=
ng?

Another approach to producing 240 individual abundance estimates might=20
be via the Distance R package on CRAN, if you are comfortable using the=20
R scripting language.

Feel free to contact me off-list to discuss the niggly details.
